the 3-5-dicarboxy-2,4-trimethylpyrrole is the most potent porphyrogenic agent known, and that its activity is due to the twisting of its ethoxycarbonly substituents out-of-plane of its ring system.
the porphyria-induction activity of DDC is related to its nonplanarity and that the 3-5-dicarbonyl substituent of DDC is necessary for optimal induction activity.

the synthesis and evaluation of a series of compounds which are analogues of the known porphyria-inducer, 3,5diethoxycarbontyl-l,4-dlhydro-2,4.6-trlmethylpyridine.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the porphyriainducting activity of DDC and its analogues is related to the ability of the compounds to twist the ethoxycarboxylic ester groups out of the plane.
